purpose: Measure replacing two software half conversions per Q5_1 decode block with F16C, preserving arithmetic order.
success: All three experimental candidate/reference pairs meet the unchanged qualification gates and match baseline answers; target decode margin >=0.85. No released qualification is claimed.
hypothesis: Hardware conversion reduces Q5_1 decode overhead without altering finite weights or answers.
controls: Same Java Models0.5.9/Vectors0.1.32 released JARs, pinned compiler and source tree except two decode conversions and tests; native16/decode8, workload/reference16. Native binaries retain debug symbols in both variants. Separate released-default and source-native correctness smokes. Three orders frozen before launch.
limitations: One catalog RAG corpus tests this admission gate; it is not a broad quality benchmark. RAG report records output text and token counts, not token IDs. One host cannot establish cross-host performance.

fleet.stopCondition: Exit on completion or error, terminate-on-shutdown, 150 minute hard shutdown

nativeSourceComparison: Baseline native source matches v0.5.9 except package version metadata; candidate differs by F16C conversions and tests.
